transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Great Sage. The Queen Mother's garden keepers found thirty-seven half-eaten peach pits beneath the ancient tree. Your paw prints are all over the branches. You were explicitly forbidden to enter. Have you no explanation for this audacity?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ha! Thirty-seven peaches, you say? I could have eaten a hundred and you'd never have known the difference! As for the paw prints, well, they're mine, all right. But 'audacity'? Hardly! I simply took what was due to me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Due to you? By what right? The Jade Emperor granted you a title and a place in Heaven, not license to plunder the Queen Mother's sacred orchard. Do you think your status as the Great Sage Equaling Heaven places you above all celestial law?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Law? Rights? Titles? Pah! I am the Great Sage Equaling Heaven, not the Great Slave Obeying Earthly Bounds. The peaches were luscious and ripened to perfection. Why should they be wasted on a select few when I could savor them? If that offends your delicate sensibilities, tough luck!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your arrogance is boundless, but it does not erase the evidence. The peaches were not yours to take. They were cultivated for the Celestial Peach Banquet, a gathering of utmost importance. Your actions have disrupted the harmony of Heaven itself. Do you truly feel no remorse?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Remorse? For what? Enjoying a bit of fruit? Your precious 'harmony' is not disturbed by my actions; it is/defined by them! I have broadened the scope of the celebration. Think of it: the peaches now include the taste of rebellion! A true ban-quet, fit for immortals and monkeys alike!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: This is not a jest, Great Sage. Your "rebellion" has consequences. The Queen Mother is furious. The Jade Emperor's patience is not infinite. Do you understand the gravity of your defiance, or do you truly believe your strength alone shields you from all reprisal?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Consequences? Gravity? Reprisal? These words are but whispers in the wind to me, Official. My strength is not just in my might, but in my spirit. If the Jade Emperor himself were to raise his hand against me, I would laugh in his face! You can try to吓唬 me with your celestial laws, but you'll find I am beyond your reach.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your spirit is indeed indomitable, but it is also reckless. You speak of being beyond reach, yet you stand here in the celestial realm, under the Jade Emperor's roof. Do not mistake tolerance for weakness. I ask you one last time, plainly: why did you break the prohibition and consume the peaches? Was it mere hunger, or a deliberate challenge to the throne?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Hunger? Challenge? Both, and neither! I am Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, and I do as I please. If the peaches were there for the taking, why not take them? It's in my nature to explore, to test, to enjoy. The prohibitions of your celestial realm mean nothing to me. I respect no boundaries but my own. If you seek a reason, look no further than my very essence: I am chaos, I am freedom, and I am beyond your understanding!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Then you leave me no choice but to report your words, unrepentant and defiant, directly to the Jade Emperor. Your "essence" of chaos will be met with order, Great Sage. The heavens will not be mocked. Guards will be posted, and you will be watched. Consider this your final warning.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Watch me? Ha! I welcome it! Let your guards be as numerous as the stars in the sky! I shall baffle and confound them all. As for your threats, they are as ineffectual as a pebble thrown at the moon. I have danced with tigers and dueled with dragons. What have you to offer that can truly threaten the Great Sage Equaling Heaven? Go, report. The Jade Emperor will find me more amusing than he could have imagined.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: So be it. Your amusement will be short-lived. The celestial court does not operate on whimsy. Your defiance is noted, and the consequences will follow. May you find your freedom worth the price you are about to pay.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Price? Consequences? You think me a simpleton to be swayed by such words? The price is always worth it when you stand by your nature! I have already paid more than you could ever imagine. I have suffered the Great Vehicle, the golden cangue, and the binding spell. If a few peaches are all it takes to rouse your ire, then let us see what the heavens can truly mete out to the Monkey King. I await your best with open arms!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your bravado is noted, Great Sage. But the heavens do not merely mete out punishment; they restore balance. You will see. Your open arms may yet find themselves bound by more than your pride. The report will be made.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Restore balance? As if the universe were a scale to be balanced with a few peaches! Your quaint ideas of order and balance are as laughable as a turtle trying to outswim a dragon. I will meet your restored balance with a force of nature that will make the celestial realm shudder! Go, report, and let us see if your threats can stand against the might of the Great Sage Equaling Heaven!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Enough. Your words are recorded. The might of the Great Sage will be measured against the will of Heaven. We shall see who trembles. The audience is over.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Audience? It seems I have been granted an audience with you, Official. I would have preferred a more spirited debate, but I suppose the grand celestial stage is yet to be set. Until then, I shall anticipate with great eagerness the show that is to come. Will the heavens shrink from my might? Will the Monkey King succumb to your 'restoration'? Only time will tell. Until we meet again, fare you well!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, Great Sage. May your anticipation be tempered by wisdom before it is too late. The stage is indeed set, and the next act will not be of your choosing.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Tempered by wisdom? Such counsel is wasted on me! The stage is always of my choosing, for I am the playwright, the actor, and the audience rolled into one. Your warnings are as ineffective as a lion warning a mouse not to enter its den. The act is about to commence, and the Great Sage will take center stage, no matter how much you seek to dim the lights. Prepare yourself, for the show will be more magnificent than you can imagine!
